sentence: This project tries to find out what keeps the cornea, the outer layer of the eye, healthy and how it repairs itself.
This project studies infectious diseases in children, including their fundamental biology, diagnosis, prevention and treatment.
This project works to find the cause of undiagnosed diseases and to build tools that help doctors find people with undiagnosed conditions.
This project builds computer vision tools that spot and grade dysplasia in inflammatory bowel disease on colonoscopy and histology.
This project tries to find out how to keep telomerase RNA molecules stable in hematopoietic cells of patients with bone marrow failure.
This project studies how cell forces shape the development of the meniscus, a part of the knee.
This project tests whether channels in endothelial cells control how arteries contract, and whether this fails during hypertension.
This project studies how immune cells called neutrophils cause inflammation and scarring in primary sclerosing cholangitis, a liver disease.
This project studies lysine methylation across the lifecycle of human papillomavirus and how the virus interacts with its host.
This project studies how RNA viruses like influenza adapt, and how protein folding machinery in host cells shapes that adaptation.
This project builds a platform that automates sample preparation for mass spectrometry of biotherapeutics.
This project focuses on regenerative and stem cell-based therapies that can replenish organs, tissues, or cells damaged by disease.
This project works to prevent and control bacterial pneumonia, invasive bacterial diseases, respiratory viruses and fungal infections using genomic epidemiology.
This project studies how epigenetic modifications, transcription and developmental potential are linked across stem cell states.
This project supports a high-level biosafety laboratory and develops models of disease to help respond to a public health emergency.
This project studies how the brain of Botryllus schlosseri, a long-lived invertebrate, develops, regenerates and ages.
This project studies the postmortem brains of people with posttraumatic stress disorder and depression to find molecular pathways.
This project tries to make genetic testing for cardiovascular disease more accurate by building a risk prediction method.
This project tests whether targeting integrins on myeloid cells helps pancreas cancer respond to immunotherapy.
This project studies how granulosa cells move to form follicles around developing oocytes and how the physical environment of the ovary affects this.
